title: Tramell Jones Gets the Call: Buddy Martin Show Panel Backs Sumrall's QB Decision Before Oklahoma
excerpt: The quarterback question that hung over Gainesville all week was the focus of Thursday night's Buddy Martin Show, where the panel backed what it viewed as Jon Sumrall's call.

blocks.text: The quarterback question that hung over Gainesville all week was the focus of Thursday night's Buddy Martin Show, where the panel backed what it viewed as Jon Sumrall's call.

runs.t: The quarterback question that hung over Gainesville all week was the focus of Thursday night's Buddy Martin Show, where the panel backed what it viewed as Jon Sumrall's call.

blocks.text: The panel treated Tramell Jones Jr. as Florida's call at quarterback. Loren Meadows, on with Buddy from the top of the show, did not hedge.

runs.t: The panel treated Tramell Jones Jr. as Florida's call at quarterback. Loren Meadows, on with Buddy from the top of the show, did not hedge.

blocks.text: "I think it was the right call," Meadows said. "Because I think with Florida's situation at that position, I think Tramell Jones gives you the better chance to win than Aaron Philo does."

runs.t: "I think it was the right call," Meadows said. "Because I think with Florida's situation at that position, I think Tramell Jones gives you the better chance to win than Aaron Philo does."

blocks.text: Meadows went further, pointing at the huddle, not just the stat sheet: "The team plays better for Jones. The team wants to play for Jones."

runs.t: Meadows went further, pointing at the huddle, not just the stat sheet: "The team plays better for Jones. The team wants to play for Jones."

blocks.text: And when the conversation turned to the noise around the decision — the suggestion that Jones is getting the job for the wrong reasons — Meadows shut it down in the line of the night: "If this is daddy ball, then every coach in America does daddy ball."

blocks.text: Buddy made the same point from the other side of the ball: the problems run deeper than one position. "This is an offense that is underachieving," he said. "It is not just at the quarterback position."

blocks.text: Ben Troupe joined at the bottom of the hour and framed Saturday simply: give Florida a quarterback who can be "the captain of the offense and distribute the ball," and the Gators can play with Oklahoma. His game of the weekend, though, is elsewhere: Georgia-Ole Miss.

runs.t: Ben Troupe joined at the bottom of the hour and framed Saturday simply: give Florida a quarterback who can be "the captain of the offense and distribute the ball," and the Gators can play with Oklahoma. His game of the weekend, though, is elsewhere: Georgia-Ole Miss.

blocks.text: Paul Wilson Jr. closed the panel with the playoff picture. On Miami-Notre Dame, he was blunt: "Notre Dame is playing for its life." He picked a shootout, and Loren agreed — "I think it's going to be a 45 to 41 game."

runs.t: Paul Wilson Jr. closed the panel with the playoff picture. On Miami-Notre Dame, he was blunt: "Notre Dame is playing for its life." He picked a shootout, and Loren agreed — "I think it's going to be a 45 to 41 game."

blocks.text: On playoff expansion, the panel split. Wilson: "I think 24 teams. I think the regular season would not matter as much." Buddy's answer: "I think 16 is enough. I don't think you need 24." And on the era Florida fans grew up in, Meadows delivered the epitaph: "The days of dynasties are over. There is no dynasty anymore."
